item.content:encoded:
Motor racing-Nike to become Formula One's official apparel and uniform partner Formula One's push to turn its rapid global growth into a broader lifestyle business took another step on Thursday with the announcement of a long-term partnership that will make Nike the sport's official apparel and uniform supplier from 2027. Reuters | Updated: 20-11-2026 06:39 IST | Created: 20-11-2026 06:39 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Formula One's push to turn its rapid global growth into a broader lifestyle business took another step on Thursday with the announcement of a long-term partnership that will make Nike the sport's official apparel and uniform supplier from 2027. Nike will create co-branded uniforms for staff at Formula One events worldwide, as well as footwear, apparel and accessories for fans. Financial terms were not disclosed. The partnership will also cover F1 Academy, Formula One's all-female development series, where Nike will provide performance-focused apparel and support athlete innovation initiatives. The collaboration will make its first public appearance with a limited Las Vegas Grand Prix x Nike capsule collection, available on Friday at the F1 Hub and Nike stores in Las Vegas ahead of the Saturday night race. Formula One has increasingly pursued partnerships beyond traditional motorsport categories as it seeks to engage younger audiences and extend its appeal across fashion, entertainment and culture. "Formula 1 is experiencing unprecedented global growth," Formula One President and Chief Executive Stefano Domenicali said in a statement, describing Nike as an ideal partner for the championship's next phase. Nike President and Chief Executive Elliott Hill said Formula One's emphasis on competition, speed and innovation matched the sportswear company's athlete-focused approach. "Together, we have an incredible opportunity to bring new energy to the sport, serve its athletes and inspire fans around the world," Hill said.

item.content:encoded:
Anthropic makes Nasdaq debut after record USD 81 billion IPO, secures USD 1.5 trillion valuation Artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic, the developer of the Claude chatbot, made its Nasdaq debut on Thursday following a record USD 81.34 billion initial public offering (IPO), securing a valuation of approximately USD 1.5 trillion, according to Reuters. ANI | Updated: 19-11-2026 20:47 IST | Created: 19-11-2026 20:47 IST

Anthropic made its Nasdaq debut on Thursday. (Photo:Nasdaq). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic, the developer of the Claude chatbot, made its Nasdaq debut on Thursday following a record USD 81.34 billion initial public offering (IPO), securing a valuation of approximately USD 1.5 trillion, according to Reuters. The landmark public offering comes amid growing investor interest in artificial intelligence companies, even as concerns persist over elevated valuations, the sustainability of AI-related investments and the potential emergence of a market bubble. According to the company's IPO details, Anthropic offered 980 million shares at USD 83 apiece, raising approximately USD 81.34 billion through the public offering. The company is listed on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the proposed ticker symbol 'ANT'. Reuters reported that the record IPO represents a major test of Wall Street's confidence in the AI boom, as investors weigh the technology's potential to transform the global economy against concerns over financial risks and its broader implications for humanity. The offering also comes alongside the latest earnings announcement from AI chipmaker Nvidia, with both developments serving as significant indicators of investor confidence in the rapidly expanding artificial intelligence industry. According to the financial details provided in the IPO filing, Anthropic reported revenue of USD 33.24 billion, while its net loss stood at approximately USD 104.04 billion. The company reported total assets of USD 154.32 billion and total liabilities of USD 146.68 billion, highlighting the scale of its financial operations. Anthropic, led by Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei, had approximately 5,300 employees as of September 30, 2026. The IPO details also showed that the company had approximately 7.43 billion shares outstanding, while the offering included around 23.65 million shareholder shares. The record listing marks a significant milestone for the artificial intelligence industry, with Anthropic's market valuation placing it among the world's most highly valued technology companies. (ANI)

item.title: US jobless claims rise by 1,000 to 203,000, continuing claims climb by 70,000
item.description: The number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment benefits rose by 1,000 to a seasonally adjusted 203,000 in the week ended November 14, while the number continuing to receive benefits ...
item.content:encoded:
US jobless claims rise by 1,000 to 203,000, continuing claims climb by 70,000 The number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment benefits rose by 1,000 to a seasonally adjusted 203,000 in the week ended November 14, while the number continuing to receive benefits climbed by 70,000 to 1.763 million in the preceding week, the US Department of Labor said on Thursday. ANI | Updated: 19-11-2026 19:41 IST | Created: 19-11-2026 19:41 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment benefits rose by 1,000 to a seasonally adjusted 203,000 in the week ended November 14, while the number continuing to receive benefits climbed by 70,000 to 1.763 million in the preceding week, the US Department of Labor said on Thursday. “In the week ending November 14, the advance figure for seasonally adjusted initial claims was 203,000, an increase of 1,000 from the previous week's revised level,” the department said in its weekly unemployment insurance claims report. It revised the previous week’s figure up to 202,000 from 200,000. The four-week moving average of initial claims, which smooths out weekly fluctuations, rose by 2,000 to 197,750 from a revised 195,750. Initial claims, which track new applications for unemployment benefits, were below the 222,000 recorded in the comparable week a year earlier. “The advance number for seasonally adjusted insured unemployment during the week ending November 7 was 1,763,000, an increase of 70,000 from the previous week's revised level,” the department said. It revised the prior week’s figure down to 1.693 million from 1.697 million. Continuing claims count people who remain on unemployment benefits after an initial week of aid. The figures are reported with a one-week lag relative to initial claims. Their four-week average rose by 10,250 to 1.717 million, while the weekly figure remained below the 1.949 million recorded a year earlier. Before seasonal adjustment, new claims under state programmes fell by 11,941, or 5.7 per cent, to 197,492 in the week ended November 14. The department said seasonal patterns had pointed to a decline of 12,534, or 6 per cent. The seasonally adjusted insured unemployment rate, which measures the share of workers covered by unemployment insurance who are receiving benefits, held at 1.1 per cent in the week ended November 7, compared with 1.3 per cent a year earlier. (ANI)
